title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Capacitor — 2024
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Define capacitance. Derive the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor.
questions.solution:
**Capacitance** C = Q/V: charge stored per unit voltage. SI unit: **farad (F)**.

Two plates of area A, separation d, charge ±Q: field E = σ/ε₀ = Q/(Aε₀). Potential V = Ed = Qd/(Aε₀).

C = Q/V = **ε₀A/d**. With a dielectric of constant εᵣ filling the gap: C = εᵣε₀A/d.
questions.knowledgeNote: 1 F is enormous — real capacitors live in the pF–mF range, so NEB answers in μF/pF are a sanity check.
questions.answer: **Definition:** capacitance C = Q/V — the charge stored per unit potential difference; SI unit the **farad** (1 F = 1 C/V). **Derivation:** plates of area A, separation d, charge Q, surface density σ = Q/A. (1) By Gauss's law the field between the plates is E = σ/ε₀ = Q/(ε₀A) (the two plates' fields add in the gap, cancel outside); (2) for a uniform field V = Ed = Qd/(ε₀A); (3) C = Q/V = **ε₀A/d** (with dielectric K: C = Kε₀A/d). **Deep point:** the formula contains neither Q nor V — capacitance is geometry (area up, gap down), not charge.

questions.question: A parallel plate air capacitor has plates of area 0.04 m² separated by 2 mm. Calculate its capacitance. (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F/m)
questions.knowledgeNote: C ∝ A/d — doubling the plate area or halving the gap doubles the capacitance.
questions.answer: **Formula:** C = ε₀A/d (air). **Substitute:** A = 0.04 m²; d = 2 mm = 2 × 10⁻³ m. C = (8.85 × 10⁻¹² × 0.04)/(2 × 10⁻³) = (3.54 × 10⁻¹³)/(2 × 10⁻³) = **1.77 × 10⁻¹⁰ F ≈ 177 pF**. **Deep point:** the pF scale is the everyday reality of air capacitors — ε₀'s tiny value means practical capacitances live in picofarads unless area is huge or a high-K dielectric is used.

questions.question: Capacitors of 2 μF and 3 μF are connected (i) in series and (ii) in parallel. Find the equivalent capacitance in each case.
questions.solution:
(i) Series: 1/C = 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6 → C = **1.2 μF** (series is always smaller than the smallest).

(ii) Parallel: C = 2 + 3 = **5 μF**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Capacitors combine oppositely to resistors: series shrinks, parallel adds — mixing them up is the standard trap.
questions.answer: **(i) Series:** 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ = 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6 ⟹ C = 6/5 = **1.2 μF** (smaller than either — series reduces capacitance, same charge on each). **(ii) Parallel:** C = C₁ + C₂ = 2 + 3 = **5 μF** (larger than either — parallel adds plate area, same voltage on each). **Deep point:** series and parallel capacitors combine opposite to resistors — memorise it as 'capacitors add in parallel, reciprocals add in series', and check the sanity: series must come out below the smallest, parallel above the largest.

questions.question: A 12 μF capacitor is charged to 100 V. How much energy is stored in it?
questions.knowledgeNote: U = ½CV² = Q²/2C = ½QV — pick the form matching the given pair (C,V), (C,Q), or (Q,V).
questions.answer: **U = ½CV²** = ½ × 12 × 10⁻⁶ × (100)² = ½ × 12 × 10⁻⁶ × 10⁴ = 6 × 10⁻² J = **0.06 J**. **Deep point:** same arithmetic as any ½CV² question — convert μF to F first, and the volts squared does the scaling.

questions.question: What is a dielectric? Explain how inserting a dielectric slab increases the capacitance of a capacitor.
questions.solution:
A **dielectric** is an insulating material whose molecules polarise in an electric field.

The induced surface charges oppose the plate charges, weakening the internal field E. Since V = Ed falls while Q stays fixed, C = Q/V **rises by the dielectric constant εᵣ** (C = εᵣC₀).
questions.knowledgeNote: Battery connected (V fixed) vs isolated (Q fixed) give opposite energy answers — always check which is held constant.
questions.answer: **Dielectric:** an insulating material (paper, mica, glass, ceramic) placed between capacitor plates; its molecules have no free charges but polarise in a field. **How it increases capacitance:** when the slab fills the gap, its molecules polarise — positive ends face the negative plate and vice versa — producing an **induced internal field opposite to the applied field**. The net field inside falls to E/K (K = dielectric constant > 1), so the potential difference for the *same charge* falls to V/K; since C = Q/V and Q is unchanged, **C rises to K times its air value**: C = Kε₀A/d. (Equivalently, at constant V the polarised surface charges let the plates hold K times more charge.) **Deep point:** the dielectric never conducts — it *screens*: the induced field is the mechanism, and K is just the ratio measuring how well the material screens.

questions.question: Write any four uses of capacitors.
questions.solution: (1) Smoothing/filtering ripples in power supplies. (2) Tuning radio circuits (with an inductor). (3) Storing the firing energy in camera flashes and defibrillators. (4) Power-factor correction in factories; (5) blocking DC while passing AC between amplifier stages.
questions.knowledgeNote: Every use exploits one property: capacitors store charge, block DC, and pass AC.
questions.answer: **Four uses of capacitors:** (1) **storing charge/energy** — camera flash, defibrillators, SMPS filters; (2) **smoothing/filtering** in power supplies (rectifier output → steady DC); (3) **tuning circuits** in radios (variable capacitor sets the resonant frequency); (4) **blocking DC while passing AC** — coupling stages in amplifiers; (also: time-delay circuits with resistors, motor starting, power-factor correction). **Deep point:** every use trades on one property — a capacitor stores charge in an electric field and resists sudden voltage changes.
